description: Geospatial Data from the “Building a Model to Reconstruct the Hellenistic and Roman Road Networks of the Eastern Desert of Egypt, a Semi-Empirical Approach Based on Modern Travelers’ Itineraries” Paper is a data set described in the paper "Geospatial Data from the “Building a Model to Reconstruct the Hellenistic and Roman Road Networks of the Eastern Desert of Egypt, a Semi-Empirical Approach Based on Modern Travelers’ Itineraries” Paper" in Journal of Open Archaeology Data (Ubiquity Press, 2020), produced by Louis Manière, Maël Crépy, Bérangère Redon. – Topographic factor: Digital Elevation Model. – Navigation factor: allows to discriminate valley areas (wadi) where travelers easily orient themselves from areas with few landscaped landmarks. It was produced by analyzing the theoretical hydrographic network, itself created by DEM processing. – Terrain factor: This layer represents the difficult walking zones for a loaded camel that are the coherent outcropping rocks or coarse sedimentary deposits. Coverage: the Eastern Desert of Egypt in Hellenistic and Roman times. The paper does not give a data set link that the open sources used could show, so the paper is the only link; the data location and formats need checking on the paper page, which the cloud cannot open for this journal. Licence: not stated (data set page not reachable on 2026-10-01; the paper is CC-BY-3.0). Cost: no charge is stated in the metadata read; the paper's own access terms were not checked. Caveats: written from the paper's abstract and metadata only, so contents, quality and current availability are unchecked and the description may lag the source. It can support historical road network and least-cost path modelling. Related: the paper is the Journal of Open Archaeology Data article 10.5334/joad.71.
